newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada spot natgas prices stay weak in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Canada spot natgas prices stay weak in quiet trade.

text.p: Canadian domestic spot natural gas prices remained at recent weak levels in quiet Wednesday trade, despite cold weather in western Canada.
Traders said the current AECO price of about C$1.40 per gigajoule for nearly all terms was sending a strong signal that the market was headed for an early downturn.
Gas at the AECO hub was quoted at the level for spot, April and summer trade. Last week, spot AECO fetched US$1.50/1.53 per GJ.
"I think this is the last hurrah for gas prices," said a Calgary-based trader.
"When its -23 (Celsius) and the gas price doesn't move, I think the writing's on the wall."
Southern Alberta temperatures had dropped this week to those lows (-9 Fahrenheit), but above-normal temperatures were forecast for the weekend.
Storage gas in Alberta was said to have been withdrawn at an average rate this week of 300 million cubic feet per day.
Most export prices were slightly stronger than last week.

Gas at Sumas, Wash. was talked at about US$1.25 per million British thermal units, up about 20 cents on the week, amid cooler temperatures in the U.S. Pacific northwest and a draw on linepack on Westcoast Energy Inc's intra-British Columbia pipeline system.
Prices for gas destined for U.S. Midwest markets climbed about four cents from last week as storage demand in the region climbed after a light March bidweek.
Niagara gas eased about one cent from February 26. One trader of eastern gas spot prices in southern Ontario were closely tracking NYMEX fluctuations.
